source_title: 1.2 lakh electors deleted in Kolkata; West Bengal Congress asks poll body for corrective steps before civic polls
source_excerpt: Kolkata West Bengal Congress leaders on Friday (October 30, 2026) flagged that 1.20 lakh electors from Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and 39,000 from Howrah were removed from electoral rolls; they urged the poll body to take corrective measures to restore all rightful voters before the civic body polls. “Around 1, 20,000 voters shall not be able to cast their votes in the upcoming Kolkata Municipal Corporation and 39,000 voters in the Howrah Municipal Corporation due to the issues of logical discrepancies in relation to the unplanned SIR process which are hanging in the tribunal. We sincerely request your intervention for immediate follow up and priority basis disposal,” the letter said. Authority of officials who appealed against inclusion of names in Bengal SIR under lens Authority of officials who appealed against inclusion of names in Bengal SIR under lens The officials who filed appeals against the inclusion of the 16.10 lakh voters may not have had the authority to do so under the Representation of the People Act; according to the Act, the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are the authorities with respect to electoral rolls Election Commission’s appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions storyline 1 The letter was also sent to the Chief Electoral Officer (West Bengal), the State Election Commissioner, and Municipal Commissioner and Administrator of KMC. “Over 1.59 lakh people will miss their votes; why are their cases not being heard on a priority basis at the tribunals? They missed exercising their voting rights one time during Vidhan Sabha; this is a repeated violation of people’s democratic right,” Congress State general secretary Ashutosh Chatterjee, who was one of the signatories of the letter told The Hindu. Mr. Chatterjee added that they had raised the issue of wrongful deletion multiple times during the Special Intensive Revision process in West Bengal but did not get a response to any of them. Fate of voters deleted during SIR hangs in balance for upcoming municipal polls in Kolkata Fate of voters deleted during SIR hangs in balance for upcoming municipal polls in Kolkata Opposition parties as well as civil society members in West Bengal have demanded that the State Election Commission in view of the large number of eligible electors deleted from the electoral roll under SIR, consider holding elections only after the conclusion of the special re-enrolment drive and SSR Fate of voters deleted during SIR hangs in balance for upcoming municipal polls in Kolkata storyline 1 The State Congress leaders have also alleged that the claims and objections related to the delimitation process within the KMC jurisdiction are also pending with the administration, from which they have not received any communication. Two days back on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), political leaders and activists had written to the State Election Commissioner Krishna Gupta and urged them to delay the civic polls till the ongoing Special Summary Revision (SSR). Opposition leaders, activists urge SEC to delay Bengal civic polls till SSR to enrol voters is complete Opposition leaders, activists urge SEC to delay Bengal civic polls till SSR to enrol voters is complete Opposition leaders, activists urge SEC to delay Bengal civic polls till SSR to enrol voters is complete storyline 1 The draft roll of the SSR will be published on November 11, and the final roll will be out on January 16, 2027. The municipal body polls are likely to be held in KMC, HMC, and several other municipalities in the next few weeks. The dates are yet to be announced. The memorandum submitted also said that the majority of the appeals filed at the tribunals from Kolkata and Howrah had been included back in the lists, and that rightful leaders should not be deprived of their right to vote. The letter was signed by MP Saugata Roy, Congress State president Subhankar Sarkar, former Rajya Sabha MP Jawhar Sircar, and several others. EOM
